result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_node_connectivity_between()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute node connectivity between two nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L25316-L25396){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_node_connectivity_between( source, target, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Node connectivity between two nodes](/assets/graphs/get-node-connectivity-between.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Two diamonds that share the hub node D, with B and E outlined as source and target. Every path from B to E passes through the accent hub D, so one node removal separates them. The card shows the cut D and the value 1." width="100%"} Returns the minimum number of nodes that must be removed to disconnect the source from the target. Uses Menger's theorem: this equals the maximum number of node-disjoint paths between the nodes. Implementation transforms the graph by splitting each internal node into in-node and out-node with capacity 1, converting node connectivity to edge connectivity, which is computed using max-flow. Time complexity: `O(V * E^2)` using Ford-Fulkerson with BFS. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Source node ID (int) or label (str). [target]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Target node ID (int) or label (str). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Minimum number of nodes whose removal disconnects source from target. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If source or target doesn't exist, or if source == target. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} On a path graph, the two endpoints are only connected through the interior nodes, so removing any single one of them severs the connection: ::: {#be128634 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() for i in range(1, 6): graph.add_node(label=str(i)) for i in range(1, 5): graph.add_edge(str(i), str(i + 1)) # Returns 1 (any middle node disconnects them) graph.get_node_connectivity_between("1", "5") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 1 ``` ::: ::: Node IDs work just as well as labels: ::: {#9bf0e26e .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} node1_id = graph.get_id_from_label("1") node5_id = graph.get_id_from_label("5") # Returns 1 graph.get_node_connectivity_between(node1_id, node5_id) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 1 ``` ::: ::: In a complete graph `K_5`, every pair of nodes has 4 node-disjoint paths between them, since there are 4 other nodes each offering an alternate route: ::: {#8de20182 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() for i in range(1, 6): graph.add_node(label=str(i)) for i in range(1, 6): for j in range(i + 1, 6): graph.add_edge(str(i), str(j)) # Returns 4 (need to remove 4 nodes to disconnect) graph.get_node_connectivity_between("1", "5") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 4 ``` ::: :::
